SAMUEL ACHTERBERG-OSEI
Cloud Infrastructure Engineer | Azure | Terraform | DevOps
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Cloud infrastructure engineer with experience designing and operating Azure environments, building infrastructure as code with Terraform, and automating application delivery with Azure DevOps. Hands-on experience with Azure networking, AKS operations, virtual machines, PowerShell automation, and practical Microsoft 365 security baselines. Delivered a 60-server VMware-to-Azure migration without unplanned downtime and helped increase deployment frequency for internal applications from roughly monthly to several times per week.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: Microsoft Azure, Azure IaaS, Azure Migrate, Azure VMs, Azure Firewall, virtual networks, VNet peering, private DNS, private endpoints, site-to-site VPN
Infrastructure as code and automation: Terraform, Terraform module testing with Terratest, drift detection, PowerShell
Platform and delivery: Azure DevOps Pipelines, YAML pipelines, AKS operations (upgrades, node pools, ingress), Docker, Helm, App Service
Systems and security: Windows and Linux servers, VMware, Microsoft 365, Entra ID, MFA, Conditional Access, mailbox auditing, backups
Programming and scripting: PowerShell; Python (small scripts); Go (Terratest tests)

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Cloud Engineer (Contract) | Havenstad Logistics | 2025–Present
- Build and operate Azure infrastructure, Terraform modules, Azure DevOps pipelines, and AKS environments.
- Developed a hub-and-spoke Azure network across three subscriptions, including Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints for storage and SQL, and VNet peering.
- Added Terratest module tests to the pipeline and set up a nightly infrastructure drift-detection job.
- Replaced manual deployments for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps YAML pipelines for build, test, and deployment to App Service or AKS.
- Helped increase deployment frequency from roughly monthly to several times per week for most applications.
- Operate AKS upgrades, node pools, and ingress; application manifests are owned by developers.

Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services | 2014–2020
- Administered Windows and Linux servers and supported IT services in a municipal environment.
- Planned and executed the migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate.
- Completed the cut-over over six weekends with no unplanned downtime.
- Worked with Azure VMs, VNets, site-to-site VPN, and PowerShell automation.

Freelance IT Support | 2022–2023
- Created a repeatable PowerShell script and checklist for small-business Microsoft 365 security baselines.
- Enabled MFA, Conditional Access, mailbox auditing, and backups for small clients.

CAREER BREAKS AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
Career break | Mar 2020–Aug 2022
- Took time away from paid work to provide full-time care for a family member.
- Kept Azure Administrator Associate knowledge current and provided unpaid IT help to church and family.

Professional development | Feb 2024–Feb 2025
- Completed a three-month, part-time, online English-language cloud bootcamp in Dec 2024.
- Built a Proxmox homelab and studied Terraform; passed the Terraform Associate certification in 2025.

SELECTED PROJECTS
Azure Landing Zone Networking | Havenstad Logistics | 2025
- Built a Terraform hub-and-spoke network across three Azure subscriptions, with Azure Firewall, private DNS zones, private endpoints for storage and SQL, and VNet peering.
- Added Terratest module tests to the pipeline and a nightly drift-detection job.

Release Pipelines for Internal Apps | Havenstad Logistics | 2025–2026
- Replaced manual deployment processes for 15 internal .NET and Node applications with Azure DevOps YAML pipelines covering build, test, and deployment to App Service or AKS.
- Increased deployment frequency from roughly monthly to several times per week for most applications.

VMware to Azure Migration | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services | 2019
- Planned and executed the migration of 60 servers to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate; completed cut-over over six weekends without unplanned downtime.

Small-business Microsoft 365 Security Baseline | Freelance | 2022–2023
- Developed a reusable PowerShell script and checklist covering MFA, Conditional Access, mailbox auditing, and backups.

CERTIFICATIONS
- Azure Administrator Associate
- Terraform Associate (2025)

TRAINING
- Cloud bootcamp, part-time and online; completed Dec 2024

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with a clear Azure/DevOps positioning, relevant quantified achievements, and credible technical detail. The 60-server migration, three-subscription network, 15 application pipelines, Terratest testing, drift detection, and deployment-frequency improvement provide useful evidence of impact. The career break is explained professionally and the document is generally concise and readable. The main content weakness is that it does not explicitly show the candidate's leadership of the migration, despite that evidence appearing in the original candidate information. It also repeats the strongest Havenstad and migration achievements in both Professional Experience and Selected Projects; this is acceptable, but the repetition could be reduced if space is needed.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses standard section headings, plain text formatting, conventional chronology, searchable technology names, and no tables, graphics, or complex columns. Keyword coverage is strong for Azure, Terraform, Azure DevOps, AKS, networking, PowerShell, Linux, VMware, virtual machines, and security. AI screening probability is high for Azure infrastructure and DevOps roles, but moderate for this specific vacancy because the document does not contain supported evidence for Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, stakeholder engagement, or technical proposal leadership. Those terms should not be added as skills because they are not supported by the original candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns strongly with hands-on cloud infrastructure engineering, Azure environment design and operation, Terraform, networking, practical security, Linux, and virtual machines. The hub-and-spoke network, Azure Firewall, private endpoints, VPN, AKS operations, and Azure Migrate experience are particularly relevant to the role's infrastructure and reliability focus. The candidate's Azure experience is acceptable under the advert's 'AWS or another major cloud' wording. The candidate material explicitly states no AWS or GCP experience, so AWS is a gap rather than a CV defect. Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, IoT or automotive/remote-device integration, JVM/backend development, and demonstrated stakeholder engagement are not supported by the candidate material and should not be claimed. The document also underplays the supported evidence that the candidate led the 60-server migration. There is no direct evidence of train, fleet, telemetry, or remote-device integration, but these are genuine experience gaps and cannot be fixed through wording.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR BUT MEANINGFUL ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Systems Administrator experience section under Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services, change "Planned and executed the migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate" to "Led the planning and execution of the migration of 60 servers from VMware to Azure IaaS using Azure Migrate." This accurately reflects the original candidate information and better supports the requirement for leading technical topics.
2. In the same Maasbrug experience section, add the supported scale from the original candidate information to the first bullet: "Administered approximately 250 Windows and Linux servers and supported IT services across several municipal services." This gives recruiters stronger evidence of infrastructure scope and systems experience.
3. In the Professional Summary, strengthen the leadership evidence without claiming unsupported stakeholder management. For example, change the opening to: "Cloud infrastructure engineer with hands-on experience designing and operating Azure environments, building infrastructure as code with Terraform, automating application delivery with Azure DevOps, and leading a 60-server VMware-to-Azure migration." Keep the existing quantified delivery and migration outcomes after this sentence.
4. In the Core Skills section, retain "Terraform" and the specific supported testing and drift-detection capabilities, but do not add "Terragrunt," "mTLS," "SSL/TLS," AWS, or IoT because the original candidate information does not support them.
5. If space is limited, reduce duplication between Professional Experience and Selected Projects rather than adding unsupported keywords. Keep the quantified outcomes in Professional Experience and use Selected Projects only for the most technically distinctive details, such as the three-subscription network, Terratest, and nightly drift detection.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear positioning for Azure infrastructure and DevOps work. The summary is specific and quantified, and the experience bullets demonstrate credible delivery outcomes: a 60-server migration without unplanned downtime, Terraform module testing, drift detection, and increased deployment frequency. The chronology is transparent, including both career breaks and professional development. The main content weakness is duplication: the Selected Projects section repeats much of the Professional Experience content. The document also does not explicitly demonstrate stakeholder engagement, systems-design ownership, or secure device-to-cloud communication, although some related infrastructure experience is present.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible in its plain-text structure, conventional headings, keyword-rich skills section, and use of searchable terms such as Azure, Terraform, Azure DevOps, AKS, Docker, Helm, Azure Migrate, Linux, VMware, networking, MFA, and Conditional Access. It should parse well because it contains no tables, columns, graphics, or unusual formatting. AI screening probability is strong for Azure infrastructure, Terraform, DevOps, migration, networking, and platform operations roles. Screening performance for this specific role will be reduced by the absence of Terragrunt, mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, AWS, IoT, and explicit systems architecture or stakeholder-management language. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than terms that should be added without evidence. The [EMAIL] and [PHONE] placeholders also make the CV appear unfinished and could impair recruiter usability.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows a strong match for hands-on Azure infrastructure engineering, cloud environment design and operation, Terraform-based infrastructure as code, networking, practical security, Linux, and virtual machines. The Azure landing-zone networking project is particularly relevant to the role's architecture and platform scope. The CV is less aligned with the role's specific requirements for strong Terragrunt skills, mTLS and SSL/TLS, certificate management, IoT or remote-device integration, AWS, and JVM/backend development. The candidate information also does not establish direct experience agreeing interfaces with external manufacturers, leading cross-functional technical proposals, or bringing stakeholders along. Azure is an acceptable major-cloud background according to the advertisement, so the lack of AWS is a gap but not disqualifying. The document's clear, outcome-focused writing supports the communication requirement, but it provides limited direct evidence of stakeholder communication or technical decision leadership.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL:
1. In the contact line at the top of the CV, replace [EMAIL] and [PHONE] with the candidate's actual professional email address and phone number before submitting. Keep the LinkedIn URL in full, using a standard readable URL.

2. In the Professional Experience section under "Systems Administrator | Maasbrug Gemeente IT Services," change "Completed the cut-over over six weekends with no unplanned downtime" to "Completed the cutover over six weekends without unplanned downtime" for grammatical accuracy and professionalism.

MEANINGFUL ENHANCEMENTS:
3. Reduce duplication between Professional Experience and Selected Projects. Keep the detailed achievement bullets under each job, and either remove Selected Projects or retain only the two most relevant projects with one concise bullet each. Do not repeat the same hub-and-spoke, pipeline, migration, and deployment-frequency details in both sections.

4. In the Professional Summary, make the strongest supported match to the advertisement more explicit by changing the opening to: "Cloud infrastructure engineer with hands-on experience in Azure infrastructure engineering, cloud environment design and operation, Terraform-based infrastructure as code, Azure DevOps delivery automation, and platform operations." Retain the quantified migration and deployment outcomes that follow.

5. In the Career Breaks and Professional Development section, remove the separate "TRAINING" section at the end and keep the cloud bootcamp only once under Professional Development. This will eliminate repetition while preserving the training information for ATS parsing.

6. In the Certifications section, use the most precise supported certification wording consistently: "Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate" only if that is the exact certificate name; otherwise retain "Azure Administrator Associate." Do not add an issuer date or credential ID unless the candidate has those details.

This is an important truthful boundary and should not be rewritten to imply application ownership. If space is needed, shorten the wording to: "Operate AKS upgrades, node pools, and ingress; developers own application manifests."

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, professional, and strongly quantified. It presents credible Azure, Terraform, networking, migration, pipeline, AKS, and security experience, with useful outcomes such as a 60-server migration without unplanned downtime and increased deployment frequency. The career breaks are explained transparently. The main content limitations are that the document does not explicitly frame the experience as systems architecture or technical proposal leadership, and the Experience and Selected Projects sections repeat several of the same achievements. Stakeholder engagement, mTLS/SSL/TLS, and Terragrunt are not evidenced, but these are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects that can be fixed through rewriting.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, plain text formatting, conventional reverse-chronological experience, and keyword-rich descriptions, so it should parse well in most ATS platforms. Relevant terms include Azure, Terraform, Azure DevOps, AKS, Azure Migrate, Azure Firewall, virtual networks, private endpoints, VPN, PowerShell, Linux, VMware, Microsoft 365, and security controls. ATS alignment would improve modestly by using the exact phrase "systems architecture" where the existing network-design evidence supports it, and by expanding "Azure Administrator Associate" to "Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate." Do not add Terragrunt, AWS, mTLS, SSL/TLS, IoT, or backend-development claims because they are not supported by the candidate information. AI screening probability is good for Azure infrastructure and DevOps roles, but moderate for this specific position because the ad heavily emphasizes Terragrunt, mTLS/SSL/TLS, stakeholder leadership, and fleet or remote-device connectivity.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document is a strong match for hands-on Azure infrastructure engineering, cloud environment design and operation, Terraform, networking, practical security, Linux, and virtual machines. Azure is explicitly acceptable because the advertisement permits another major cloud. The migration leadership and quantified delivery improvements support technical ownership and analytical thinking. The strongest gaps are Terragrunt, mTLS and SSL/TLS, AWS, IoT/automotive or remote-device integration, and backend or full-stack development. The CV also provides limited direct evidence of leading technical proposals, engaging external stakeholders, or designing train-to-cloud interfaces. These are genuine profile gaps or unverified areas and should not be invented in the CV.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES: None identified; the document does not contain clear unsupported skills, tools, certifications, or experience when cross-referenced with the supplied candidate information.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace "leading a 60-server VMware-to-Azure migration" with "leading the planning and execution of a 60-server VMware-to-Azure migration". This matches the more precise wording supported by the candidate's original material and better demonstrates technical leadership without overstating the role.
2. In the Professional Summary, revise the opening experience description to make the existing architecture evidence more explicit: change "hands-on experience designing and operating Azure environments" to "hands-on experience designing Azure network architecture and operating Azure environments". This is supported by the hub-and-spoke, firewall, private DNS, private endpoint, peering, and VPN work already documented.
3. In the Cloud Engineer role under Havenstad Logistics, change "Developed a hub-and-spoke Azure network across three subscriptions" to "Designed and built a hub-and-spoke Azure network architecture across three subscriptions". This uses the job advertisement's systems-design language while remaining grounded in the documented project.
4. In the Selected Projects section, reduce duplication with the Experience section. Retain the detailed achievement bullets under each relevant employment entry, then either remove Selected Projects or reduce each project to one concise line containing its scope and outcome. For example, retain the 15-application deployment-frequency result as a project highlight only if it is removed from the detailed role bullets; do not repeat the same full bullets in both places.
5. In the Certifications section, change "Azure Administrator Associate" to "Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate". This is supported by the original candidate information and is more recognizable to ATS systems.
6. In the Systems and security skills line, change "Microsoft 365" to "Microsoft 365 security baselines" only if the intended meaning is the documented security work; otherwise retain the current wording. The surrounding experience bullet should continue to specify MFA, Conditional Access, mailbox auditing, and backups rather than implying broader security engineering expertise.
